$comment: Committed source-bounds corpus with expected verdicts (Phase 2 task 10). ONE corpus, driven from BOTH sides: the TypeScript suite calls range-check.ts directly, and the Python indexer suite drives the same cases through the `cutdown range-check` CLI. Because there is exactly one implementation, a divergence between the two suites is a wiring bug, never a rounding disagreement — which is the whole reason a second Python implementation was rejected. This corpus is the evidence behind the Phase 0 exit criterion 'zero invalid source ranges in final renders'.

cases.name: in-bounds-mid-asset
cases.why: The ordinary case: a range comfortably inside the asset.

cases.name: ends-exactly-at-duration
cases.why: The range is half-open, so end == duration consumes the whole asset and reads nothing past it. An off-by-one here would reject every full-length range.

cases.name: minimal-one-tick-range
cases.why: The smallest legal range. Proves the non-empty rule is > and not >=.

cases.name: one-tick-past-the-end
cases.why: The exit criterion in miniature. A single tick past the duration is the defect that reaches a render as a black frame or a decode error.

cases.name: starts-at-the-duration
cases.why: A range beginning where the asset ends contains no media at all.

cases.name: empty-range
cases.why: endTicks == startTicks. JSON Schema provably cannot express this (draft 2020-12 has no cross-property inequality and tech-spec §3 forbids if/then/else), so it can only be caught here.

cases.name: inverted-range
cases.why: endTicks < startTicks. Same unexpressible inequality, opposite direction.

cases.name: audio-timebase-exactly-full-length
cases.why: 48 kHz ticks ARE sample counts. 480000 samples == 10 s == the whole 300-tick @30fps asset. Cross-timebase comparison must be exact.

cases.name: audio-timebase-one-sample-over
cases.why: A SINGLE sample past the end, across differing timebases. This is the case a float comparison silently passes — the reason the implementation cross-multiplies with BigInt.

cases.name: wrong-asset
cases.why: A range is only meaningful against its own asset; checking it against another's duration would be a coincidence, not a validation.

cases.name: negative-start
cases.why: Ticks are counts and cannot be negative.

cases.name: fractional-tick
cases.why: A fractional tick is a category error — it means someone did float-seconds arithmetic upstream, which is exactly what the rational timebase exists to prevent.

cases.name: malformed-range-missing-ticks
cases.why: The untrusted path this module exists for: a model-proposed range that is not structurally a range at all. A missing tick is a STRUCTURAL defect, not a fractional one — reporting NON_INTEGER_TICKS would send the reader hunting for float arithmetic that was never involved.

cases.name: unsafe-integer-ticks
cases.why: Above 2^53 the value was destroyed by JSON.parse before any comparison ran, so an out-of-bounds range was reported clean. The checker refuses an unrepresentable tick rather than comparing a number it knows is already wrong.

cases.name: zero-denominator-timebase
cases.why: Must be reported as an invalid timebase, never reach a division. A validator that divides by zero cannot be run over generated output.

unknownDurationCase.name: unknown-duration-fails-closed
unknownDurationCase.why: An asset whose preflight established no duration gives no bound to prove against. The only safe verdict is refusal — passing would let an unbounded range through on the strength of missing information.
